text:
anika: seeing intermittent stream resets for long-lived gRPC inference streams going through ALB in eu-west-1. ~2% of requests hit RST after ~60s. only affects the hosted edge path, not direct NLB tests.

jacob: ugh classic. ALB idle timeout is 60s by default. are these bi-directional streams with no body traffic for some time?

anika: yes, client starts a stream, server sends keepalives every ~30s but we still see resets around 60s. logs show grpc: "transport: connection error" + TLS read error: EOF.

chad: do we have an nginx/envoy between ALB and pods? buffering or connection pooling could be collapsing streams.

anika: we use envoy sidecar in front of the model pods (istio-ish). envoy config shows http2 enabled.

maria: quick checklist: 
- confirm ALB HTTP/2 frontend -> ALB->target group uses HTTP/1.1 to targets (ALB terminates HTTP/2).
- ALB has idle_timeout.timeout_seconds attribute (set to 60 by default).
- Envoy has both http2 protocol options and connection idle/timeouts.

jacob: thanks. ALB terminating HTTP/2 means keepalives from client may not translate to backend. ALB will tear idle connections after idle_timeout.

anika: ran grpcurl against ALB with --keepalive-time=20, still saw a reset at ~60s. payloads are small so there are long idle gaps.

chad: two practical fixes:
- Add aggressive keepalive pings from server to ensure ALB sees activity (but ALB may not forward HTTP/2 pings to backend).
- Or use NLB (TCP) + preserve HTTP/2 end-to-end; NLB is better for long-lived gRPC streaming.

maria: or adjust ALB idle_timeout to a higher value for the model target group. downside: connection resources hang longer.

jacob: also check Envoy's http2_connection_keepalive (or connection_manager.keepalive) and disable http1.1 upgrades if proxy incorrectly upgrades/downgrades. example envoy snippet we used: 
```yaml
http2_protocol_options:
  initial_stream_window_size: 65536
  initial_connection_window_size: 15728640
  allow_connect: false
connection_idle_timeout: 0s # disable idle close
stream_idle_timeout: 0s # disable stream close
```
(note: set to 0s to disable idle close in canary test only)

anika: interesting — our envoy config currently has stream_idle_timeout: 15s, oops. maybe that's why.

maria: also check TCP-level NAT timeouts on nodes / cloud NAT. Idle NAT mappings can expire and cause RSTs. For GCP/AWS default NAT timeouts are ~350s but some intermediate LB or firewall rules can be shorter.

jacob: FYI I ran a tcpdump on a pod and saw the RST originated from the ALB IP (10.0.45.12). that means the ALB initiated close, not pod.

anika: good catch. can we increase ALB idle_timeout to 300s for the edge-target-group for a canary?

maria: yes, we can set attribute:
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <arn> --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=300

chad: alternative: re-route streaming traffic via a dedicated NLB target group and a TCP passthrough ALB->NLB? might be heavier ops.

jacob: quick test plan:
1) Increase ALB idle_timeout to 300s for canary TG.
2) Set envoy.stream_idle_timeout=0s on canary pods.
3) Run 30m soak with synthetic streams and tcpdump.
4) If resets persist, cutover canary to NLB.

anika: assigning action to @jacob to run the modify-attribute + soak. i'll add a dashboard spike alert on RST % for the next 6h.

deploy-bot: deploy started: envoy-config-canary -> 3 pods (image: envoy:2026-02-12)

sre-bot: alert muted for stream-resets while canary in progress (:hourglass_flowing_sand:)

maria: FYI we should also add a test that simulates long idle server-to-client intervals with small pings to ensure ALB preserves connection. use grpc-client with keepalive and a real HTTP/2 probe.

chad: note for the runbook: prefer NLB/TCP if you need true end-to-end HTTP/2 without ALB termination. ALB is more convenient but can be brittle for long-lived streams.

anika: thanks all — will post results in this thread. if increases fix it we can consider rolling change for other model TGs. :thumbsup:
